A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAE-NWM work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original linear-probe experiments, navigation and generation evaluations, component ablations, and supplementary rollout analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds deterministic-regression comparisons, longer rollouts, reconstruction and computational measurements, and a failure case.

M1.justification: The proposed frozen DINOv2/RAE components, CDiT-DH backbone, time-driven gate, flow-matching objective, and representation-space rollout procedure remain unchanged. DINO-Reg is an added comparison variant, not a replacement for the proposed method.

E1.justification: SACSoN, RECON, SCAND, Matterport3D, and the navigation tasks are retained. Section 6 adds an auxiliary static encode-decode reconstruction evaluation on RECON, without action-conditioned future prediction. This modestly extends evaluated task requirements without adding a dataset or domain.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds deterministic DINO-token regression, DINO-Reg, alongside the retained GNM, NoMaD, and NWM comparators. The other existing comparator sets remain unchanged. Newly discussed works such as V-JEPA 2 are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V2 extends sequential-rollout assessment from 16 to 32 seconds and introduces static reconstruction evaluation and dynamics-forward profiling on one A800. Existing dataset splits, training settings, two-second planning evaluation, and Habitat success criteria are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially broadens diagnostic analysis: DINO-Reg isolates the transition objective, 32-second rollouts examine longer-term degradation, static reconstruction tests texture loss, profiling measures computational cost, and Appendix E.2 examines collision-induced hallucination. The previous gate, encoder, and DDT ablations are retained.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 11 explicitly identifies solid curves as medians and shading as the 25th–75th percentiles. V2 Figure 12 retains the curves and interquartile-range discussion but removes that caption explanation. This reduces reporting detail; it does not establish changed runs or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Existing table entries and plotted results are retained, but substantial new results cover DINO-Reg, 32-second rollout errors, reconstruction FID, computational cost, and failure behavior. Table 2 shows DINO-Reg slightly beating RAE-NWM on RECON RPE, 0.36 versus 0.37. Section 6 adds reconstruction FID of 4.14 for SD-VAE versus 5.47 for DINOv2+RAE. The new RECON 16-second LPIPS value of 0.458 conflicts with the retained 0.472 in Section 6, so it cannot be treated as an established performance improvement.

T1.justification: Appendix D newly provides explicit mathematical definitions for the paper-specific dynamics proportion and dynamics-to-time ratio, including the latter's stabilizing epsilon; v1 Appendix C only names these quantities. The core task formulation and flow-matching derivation are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that dense DINOv2 representations combined with gated CDiT-DH improve rollout stability and downstream navigation. V2 makes the generative, first-person focus more explicit, but retains the principal contributions and claimed benefits.

C2.justification: V2 interprets DINO-Reg as evidence that the transition objective contributes beyond representation choice, identifies collision-induced context ambiguity as a failure condition, and explicitly acknowledges the absence of fully scale-matched training. These qualify the retained account of structural stability and texture-fidelity tradeoffs.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 clarifies token-to-grid reshaping, new Appendix C documents DINO-Reg's regression objective and retained inputs, and Section 6 discloses profiling hardware and comparative dynamics-token counts. Existing architecture, optimizer, training duration, inference settings, and repository access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work replace the characterization of feature-space predecessors as discrete-token predictors with an explicit account of continuous deterministic DINO-WM. V2 adds V-JEPA 2 and Cloning Deterministic Worlds and reframes the distinction around generative first-person navigation. This substantially revises the central research positioning, beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The seven-section main narrative remains in the same order. V2 clarifies terminology, streamlines ablation and appendix explanations, rewrites the conclusion, and adds acknowledgments and a dedicated regression appendix. These are localized editorial and structural revisions.

P2.justification: V2 globally changes typography, running headers, and text-block width, resizing and redistributing figures and tables throughout. It adds DINO-Reg Figure 7, failure-case Figure 15, and a Table 2 row with an expanded caption. Existing figures remain present under matched or renumbered labels.

improvement.justification: The same-protocol DINO-Reg control strengthens attribution to the generative objective, while revised research positioning, computational measurements, and explicit failure and capacity limitations improve clarity and support. These gains are bounded by brief documentation of the new checks and the unresolved RECON 16-second LPIPS discrepancy between Sections 5.2 and 6.
